svg.title: Greece wine-growing study atlas
svg.desc: Connect the northern mainland and Peloponnese with distinct Ionian and Aegean island wine areas. Approximate study locations, not appellation boundaries. Numbers refer to the study key; a shared number connects places in one grouped lesson. 1: Naoussa. Northern mainland Greece in Imathia, west of Thessaloniki. 2: Amyndeon. Northwestern Greek Macedonia, west of Naoussa. 3: Goumenissa. Northern Greek Macedonia, northwest of Thessaloniki. 4: Rapsani. Thessaly near the southern foothills of Mount Olympus. 5: Nemea. Northeastern Peloponnese, southwest of Corinth. 6: Mantinia. The inland Arcadian plateau in the central Peloponnese. 7: Santorini. A small island group in the southern Aegean, north of Crete. 8: Crete. The long southern Greek island; several wine areas lie across it. 9: Kefalonia. An Ionian island west of mainland Greece. 10: Samos. An eastern Aegean island close to the Turkish coast.

g.text: Dots: representative places · outlines: geography, not appellation boundaries

text.tspan: Trace mainland valleys and island shores,
bringing a sense of place to the table.
